data.body:
PRE-EMPTIVE REMEDIATION before the first review, applying two defect classes that cost d8ef five rounds. I read every AC by hand rather than trusting my own keyword heuristic, which reported this ticket clean.

FIXED 1 — AC6 was the [operator-attested] trap in disguise. It required 'the change description and the follow-up record BOTH state that this relocates mass'. A Gerrit commit message and a ticket comment are both OUTSIDE the repository, and the completion verifier reads repository files ONLY — it explicitly cannot read git history. My keyword scan missed it because the AC says 'change description', not 'comment'. Split along the repo boundary: the caveat must now appear IN the new module's docstring (in-repo, and the place a future reader sizing up config.py's growth curve will actually meet it), with the commit-message half tagged [operator-attested].

FIXED 2 — AC2 was about to become FALSE. It said a seam test must assert a headroom target for llm/config.py 'which has no such guard today'. That is true right now and stops being true the moment sibling d8ef lands, because the guard I just wrote in tests/unit/test_plan_review_workflow_ops_seam.py covers config.py at the staged <= 800. Reworded: this ticket TIGHTENS that existing guard to the < 700 policy target, in the same change that creates the headroom, rather than adding a second one. This is the ordering rule the hardening epic already uses — the change that buys the headroom is the change that may assert it.

Neither would have been caught by the heuristic sweep; both came from reading the criteria as a reviewer would. Cheaper here than as review rounds three and four.
